idea.name: Custom shelving for storage totes
idea.one_liner: Build and install custom garage shelves that make black and yellow storage totes easier to access, charging by tote space.
idea.customer: Homeowners who store black and yellow totes in their garages.
idea.offer: Custom shelving units, with installation and delivery described as part of Alex's business.
idea.revenue_model: Charge per tote space; the totes are purchased separately by the customer.

key_quotes.quote: I make the shelving units for those black and yellow totes you can get at any of the big box stores.
Having a kind of a side by side before and after garage is unorganized to a clean shelf.
I was charging $40 per per tote per space and it's the same today.
It was all that was me when I wasn't working or building shelves. It's I was on Messenger.

claims.claim: Alex estimates that a $1,000 shelf costs about $150 in expenses.
claims.quote: If you think of a $1,000 shelf, the expenses on that is probably 150 bucks.

claims.claim: The host describes Alex's business as making $15,000 a month in net profit.
claims.quote: how he's able to make 15 grand a month in net profit selling custom garage shelves exclusively on Facebook Marketplace.

claims.claim: Alex says he quit his day job in May 2024 and devoted eight hours a day to the business.
claims.quote: May of 24, it got so busy, I quit the day job and did this full-time, dedicating eight hours a day instead of just my evenings to this.

claims.claim: Alex says he charged $40 per tote space and still does.
claims.quote: I was charging $40 per per tote per space and it's the same today.

claims.claim: A different listing price of 32 is suggested as a price test.
claims.quote: but I vary it also. Maybe I drop it down to 32.

claims.claim: Alex says he has buyers for both his usual and lower-priced listings, including a 25 price.
claims.quote: If I'm feeling frisky, 25, and just to kind of see the difference in the different listings, I get people for both, right?

claims.claim: The host calculates that a 4x5 shelf holds 20 totes and costs about $800 at $40 per space.
claims.quote: So a 4x5 would be 20 totes and that's like 800 bucks give or take.

claims.claim: The host separately states the 20-times-40 calculation as $800.
claims.quote: Just to do the math here, 20 times 40 is 800 bucks.

claims.claim: Alex says lifetime shelf installations are closer to 1,000 than the host's hypothetical 300.
claims.quote: Now, let's say theoretically you've delivered 300 shelves lifetime, >> probably closer to a thousand.

claims.claim: The host characterizes the business as reaching $15,000 a month in revenue.
claims.quote: So, you got to 15K a month in revenue.

claims.claim: A customer had 150 bins in storage before Alex's installation.
claims.quote: So, they were staying with grandma, but all their house 150 bins was in a storage unit.

claims.claim: Alex says he installed five 5x5 shelves for that customer.
claims.quote: I set them up with five 5x5 shelves.

claims.claim: Alex describes the installation as 25 times and 150 totes with wheels.
claims.quote: That's 25 times. That's 150 totes with wheels.

claims.claim: Alex says his record for in-person sales is a 100% close rate.
claims.quote: My record is still 100% for inperson.

acquisition_channels.details: Alex says leads came from Facebook Marketplace listings.
He also received referrals from Facebook Marketplace customers.
He experimented with boosting listings but said he did not see much success.

ideas.delivery: Alex builds the shelves, coordinates delivery, and installs them at customers' homes. Customers supply the totes.
ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR applies to handling customer and email lists, and to sharing customer details with installers.
